neighbours.label: a person or pronoun right after a conjugated 'have' (has/have/had/'ve got), whatever 'have' means, strongest when a state or action follows (has you covered, had me remove); weak after infinitive 'to have', after other verbs (made, let, saw, keep), and for things after 'have'
fire: Don't worry about the snacks, this new insurance plan has you covered for everything.
She has him wrapped around her little finger.
My manager had us rewrite the entire report before Friday.
That movie really had me crying by the end.
We've got you scheduled for the early shift tomorrow.
The teacher has them reading two chapters every night.
He had her sign the papers in front of a witness.
This weather has everyone staying indoors.
quiet: Don't worry about the snacks, this new insurance plan covers everything for you.
The coach made me run five extra laps after practice.
She keeps him wrapped around her little finger.
My manager wants to have us rewrite the entire report before Friday.
That movie really made me cry by the end.
We've got a schedule for the early shift tomorrow.
The teacher lets them read two chapters every night.
He saw her sign the papers in front of a witness.
